import re

# What if we only replace non-word characters at the boundaries?
def slugify_v1(text):
    text = text.strip().lower()
    # Replace sequences of non-alphanumeric with hyphen, but strip trailing/leading non-alphanum
    result = re.sub(r'[^a-z0-9]+', '-', text)
    return re.sub(r'^-+|-+$', '', result)

print('Test 1:', slugify_v1('  a   b  '))  
print('Test 2:', slugify_v1('C++ rocks!'))  
"

python3 -c "
import re

def slugify_fixed(text):
    text = text.strip().lower()
    # Replace sequences of non-alphanumeric chars with single hyphen
    result = re.sub(r'[^a-z0-9]+', '-', text)
    # Strip leading and trailing hyphens
    return re.sub(r'^-+|-+\$', '', result)

# All test cases
print('test_slugify_simple:', slugify_fixed('Hello World'), '== hello-world')
print('test_slugify_extra_spaces:', slugify_fixed('  a   b  '), '== a-b')
print('test_slugify_punctuation:', slugify_fixed('C++ rocks!'), '== c-rocks')
"
